title: Chippewa Valley Technical College nursing student overcomes challenges to graduate
text:
Ashley DeMuth, CEO | Menomonie Area Chamber of Commerce
Ashley DeMuth, CEO | Menomonie Area Chamber of Commerce
Nicole Bateson, a student at Chippewa Valley Technical College (CVTC), is set to graduate this month as a registered nurse. Over the past year, Bateson has managed her academic responsibilities while also being the primary support for a family member facing mental health challenges.
“It has been an emotionally, physically, and financially taxing year,” Bateson said. “To say I have been concerned for their well-being and life would not be an understatement.”
Bateson, who lives in Chippewa Falls, attended CVTC’s River Falls campus. She balanced coursework, clinical rotations, and lengthy commutes during her studies.
She credits CVTC faculty with helping her manage these demands. According to Bateson, instructors showed flexibility by rescheduling exams and accommodating absences when possible, while still maintaining academic standards required for accreditation. “I had heard a lot of praise for the nursing program at CVTC,” she said. “You want your education to be worth the money, and CVTC delivers.”
Bateson noted that feedback from clinical sites suggested CVTC students were well-prepared compared to peers from other programs. She also highlighted the supportive environment among students in her cohort: “None of us are in competition with each other. We do everything we can to support one another,” she said.
As she prepares to receive her diploma at commencement, Bateson reflects on her experiences with pride and looks forward to beginning her career as a nurse.
